# Single-arm development roadmap

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_repository.py from milestones.tsv. -->

One custom arm, one overhead RGB policy camera, joint-action demonstrations, and hosted Dream adaptation.
The prototype, illustrative rolling sample, and final rolling arm have distinct identities.

[milestones.tsv](milestones.tsv) is the only editable acceptance ledger. GitHub issues group work against these IDs.
Source inspection and local fixture verification retain their limited meaning. Hosted, learned, and physical gates need their own evidence.

## Apply the gates to the selected profile

Every profile obeys `depends_on`. Final rolling simulation and physical revisions also obey `final_profile_requires`.
RC03 precedes final-profile SA05 demonstrations; RC04 precedes final-profile SA07 uploads. Prototype work does not wait for final CAD.

SA01 freezes the next task and exact build contract. SA02 pins an isolated client. SA03 acquires and validates the externally supplied prototype asset.
The public two-coordinate rolling example is not that three-coordinate prototype or the unknown final design.

Read [Dream integration](dream-integration.md), [rolling joints](rolling-joints.md), and [architecture](architecture.md) for ownership and interface details.

## Preserve acceptance while trimming legacy planning

SA04 must preserve one bus owner, finite bounded inputs, ownership generations, expiry, position/velocity/acceleration/lead/effort limits, final-release checks, fault latching, takeover, and continued local control during inference delay.
Reconcile the independently developed controller and its accepted evidence before reuse. The remaining C13-C16 effort prediction, latched-fault, measured-loop/timing, and station-independence/no-auto-rearm obligations remain required.

SA05-SA06 retain bounded teleoperation, key/deadman release, focus loss, gamepad unplug/reconnect without auto-resume, controlled-timebase tests, camera timestamps/freshness, measured/requested/accepted/issued distinctions, metadata-first recording, interrupted-episode finalization/recovery, synchronized replay, provenance, hashes, and whole-episode held-out splits.

SA07-SA10 retain actual service/body acceptance, processed timing inspection, reviewed funding/prices, one initial training submission, persistent job identity, published checkpoint, no-actuation inference, and held-out closed-loop evaluation.
The policy must reobserve and respond to target shifts. Scripted paths, offline losses, and the 90-frame calibration fixture cannot pass learned-task gates.

Inject stale frames, wrong shape/units/build, NaN/Inf, delayed/reordered replies, unavailable joints, network failure, expired targets, faults, ownership changes, and takeover. Verify the build-specific supported stop/hold response; stopping a gravity-loaded arm is not necessarily torque release.

SA11-SA14 retain build-specific identity, calibrated signs/zeros/limits, routing/timing, attached mass/COM, FK/load/gravity validation, supported startup/shutdown, bounded tracking, tool/workspace/camera readiness, real demonstrations, and supervised trials.
Commissioning can proceed independently with explicit live scope. Policy readiness cannot be inferred from simulated results. Only joints needed by the accepted task-capable build must exist; absent future wrists/scoop cannot become fictitious measurements.

Freeze a separate physical held-out case set, measured tolerance, timeout, and stopping criteria before SA14 trials. Report every physical attempt and intervention independently of simulated outcomes. Meet the frozen measured rule before accepting SA14 or expanding physical difficulty/duration at SA15.

## Deferred scope

MakerMods UI, direct agents, local VLA optimizer/GPU setup, inference IK, food/portion physics, and fixed six-joint completion are outside the first reaching/pushing workflow. Revisit them for an actual task or build requirement.
The [legacy archive and crosswalk](archive/README.md) preserve the old 195-item decomposition without keeping it as a second queue.
